newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai Airways cargo staff say may resume strike.
newsitem.headline: Thai Airways cargo staff say may resume strike.

text.p: Cargo workers of Thai Airways International Plc said on Thursday they may stage a new strike to protest a move by senior airline executives last week to take part in the setting up of a Thai air cargo carrier.

The Thai Airways State Employees Association said in a statement some 1,700 cargo handling workers at Bangkok airport and other airline staff would take action to oppose the decision to incorporate a new cargo airline. It did not elaborate.

"Thai Airways cargo workers walked out of their jobs for two days early this month to force the government to stop a plan to launch the proposed cargo airline in which Thai Airways would have held a 40 percent stake."
The workers fear they may lose jobs because of the new airline.
The strike, which paralysed up to 70 percent of airport cargo movement, forced the government to announce that it would shelve the plan.

An association official told Reuters that Thai Airways president Thamnoon Wanglee and another senior executive were listed as shareholders of Thai Air Cargo Co Ltd which was incorporated on November 7, two days after the government pledged to shelve the cargo airline plan.
He said the association would hold a major meeting on Friday to decide what action it would take to express disappointment over government failure to meet its promise.
